claims.text: Retention or loss of toughness in high-entropy alloys is governed by interactions among edge dislocations, twinning, and short-range ordering.
Systematic variations in alloy composition can influence edge dislocations, twinning, and short-range ordering.
Systematic variations in processing conditions can influence edge dislocations, twinning, and short-range ordering.
The proposed behavior applies under high-stress conditions relevant to demanding engineering applications.
The proposed behavior applies under high-temperature conditions relevant to demanding engineering applications.
Interactions among edge dislocations, twinning, and short-range ordering affect the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
Interactions among edge dislocations, twinning, and short-range ordering lead to changes in toughness.
Toughness will change as a function of alloy composition or processing conditions.
Optimizing edge dislocations and twinning will increase toughness.
Minimizing short-range ordering will increase toughness.
